name: PESSRI
question: Do ring-with-support and Gellhorn pessaries differ in symptom relief and life impact for women with symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse?

design.population: 134 women with symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse of POP-Q stage II or greater, with median stage III.
design.locator: PubMed abstract; publisher Materials and Methods and Results excerpts

verdictNote: Both devices improved symptoms; the accessible report does not establish a formal equivalence threshold.
takeaway: In a randomized crossover comparison with planned three-month periods, ring-with-support and Gellhorn pessaries each improved pelvic floor symptom distress and life impact at follow-up, including early assessments when use stopped; the report found no clinically significant between-device difference in the measured scales.

reports.label: Initial crossover report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed lists April 2007; exact online publication day not verified
reports.citation: Cundiff GW, Amundsen CL, Bent AE, et al. "The PESSRI study: symptom relief outcomes of a randomized crossover trial of the ring and Gellhorn pessaries." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2007;196(4):405.e1-405.e8. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2007.02.018
reports.followUp: Three months with each assigned pessary

results.measure: PFDI scales at three months or earlier if pessary use stopped

values.ring: Statistically and clinically significant improvement on most scales
values.gellhorn: Statistically and clinically significant improvement on most scales

results.note: Clinically significant change was defined as a change greater than half the standard deviation of the pre-intervention score; the report found no clinically significant difference between the two pessaries.

results.measure: PFIQ scales at three months or earlier if pessary use stopped

values.ring: Statistically and clinically significant improvement on many scales
